title: Node.js Brotli decoding can corrupt memory and permit remote code execution
summary: Malformed Brotli input can overrun an internal decoder buffer through node:zlib, causing crashes, memory disclosure or remote code execution.

severity.rationale: The attacker must supply Brotli data that the application decompresses. Handling remote compressed content is a common runtime exposure for developer services and agents.

affected.note: Includes end-of-life lines. The Node.js notice states that end-of-life versions are affected when a security release occurs.

exposure: Relevant when Node.js applications decode attacker-controlled Brotli data with node:zlib. Check embedded runtimes separately from the command on PATH.

remediation.details: Update supported lines to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, respectively, or a later patched release on that line. Move end-of-life installations to a supported patched line. Restart dependent processes.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
